overall_summary: First-person speculative survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme planetary environment paradoxes consistently lead the channel in both total views and engagement (reaching 800-1,050+ views and 20-38 likes). Conversely, standard psychology trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and quiet science facts consistently stall below 100 views with negligible engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) achieved the highest retention-driven metrics.
winning_patterns.action: Frame high-concept planetary and space anomalies through visceral, step-by-step human survival scenarios rather than passive third-person trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,057 views, 3 comments), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views, 36 likes), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) vastly outperformed general facts.
winning_patterns.action: Hook viewers with impossible physical paradoxes (burning ice, diamond rain, pitch black darkness) within the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5 to 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' reached only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic human psychology listicles and static neuroscience facts until interactive or narrative framing can be developed.

weak_patterns.pattern: Passive Space Acoustics / Repetitive Sound Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' repeatedly capped at low view tiers (34 to 220 views across three separate attempts).
weak_patterns.action: Retire quiet/static space concepts that lack physical stakes or vivid visual payoff.
